pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING POSTURE

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.6: Reading Posture

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Reading Posture. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Identify correct reading postures in pictures or in class.
2. Identify incorrect reading postures in pictures or in class.
3. Enjoy participating in reading posture activities in class. feedback. Core-competence developed: Learning to learn, Digital literacy, Communication and collaboration

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Identify correct reading postures in pictures or in class.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify correct reading postures in pictures or in class. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Identify incorrect reading postures in pictures or in class.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify incorrect reading postures in pictures or in class. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. Enjoy participating in reading posture activities in class. feedback. Core-competence developed: Learning to learn, Digital literacy, Communication and collaboration
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to enjoy participating in reading posture activities in class. feedback. Core-competence developed: Learning to learn, Digital literacy, Communication and collaboration. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Reading Posture.
2. Explain Reading Posture to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading Posture.
4. Show that you can: Identify correct reading postures in pictures or in class.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading Posture. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Reading Posture important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Identify correct reading postures in pictures or in class.
2. Identify incorrect reading postures in pictures or in class.
3. Enjoy participating in reading posture activities in class. feedback. Core-competence developed: Learning to learn, Digital literacy, Communication and collaboration

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
